thread:
Diego: dropped a fresh prototype for the keys page. two things I want feedback on: 1) the one-time key reveal UX (too easy to miss), 2) how revoke and rotate appear in the row overflow on mobile. fig: https://design.redwood.local/mock/keys-safety-v1.png

Priya: looks nice. initial thought: make the one-time reveal panel persistent until user acknowledges. currently it disappears when you click away and that's what people miss. suggestion: show a prominent panel with heading: "Save this key now" + primary "Download key" + secondary "I saved it".

Sam: agree with persistent panel. keyboard/screen-reader flow: focus should move into the panel and land on the textarea with the key. textarea should have aria-label="New API key value, copyable" and a visible Copy button next to it. pressing Copy should set aria-live="polite" to announce "Copied to clipboard".

Irina: accessibility nit: the persistent panel must have role="dialog" and aria-modal=true if it blocks background actions. If it doesn't block, use role="region" with an accessible name. Also ensure color contrast for the yellow callout meets AA.

Maria: mobile-specific concern: overflow menu affordances are tight. on small screens revoke is dangerously close to Copy. propose grouping actions: Primary (Copy, Rename), Danger (Revoke, Rotate) separated by a divider and with larger hit areas. Also require an extra confirm for Revoke on mobile (checkbox inside modal) to prevent fat-finger mistakes.

Diego: about rotate: should rotate be reversible? we considered offering a 15s undo. pros: faster recovery. cons: might give false assurance. thoughts?

Priya: prefer reversible for 15s as toast undo. but for bulk rotate, show a combined confirmation that lists affected services and require a typed confirmation like entering "ROTATE" for bulk > 5 keys. prevents accidental mass outages.

Sam: copy proposals: primary button: "Create API key"; one-time panel heading: "Save your key (shown once)"; panel body: "This key will not be shown again. Download or copy it now." revoke modal heading: "Revoke API key" revoke body: "Revoking this key will immediately stop requests that use it." undo toast: "Key revoked \u2014 undo" (actionable).

Irina: screen-reader behavior for inline undo banner: use role="status" and aria-live="assertive" if the revoke blocks actions. If revoke is soft and clients still have grace, use polite. test with NVDA and TalkBack.

Diego: UX tiny: we currently show "Create & download" on a small button which reads oddly on narrow screens. change to "Create and download" or make a two-line label. Also add tooltip on hover: "Download this key now; it won't be visible again."

Priya: suggestion for empty state: show sample cURL that uses the key once created, so users see immediate value. e.g.,
```
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <YOUR_KEY>"
```
This can live under the CTA as a collapsible example.

Sam: tests to add to QA: keyboard-only create and download flow, toast undo announced, mobile overflow menu spacing, bulk rotate typed-confirmation path, and color-contrast for callouts.

Design-bot: automated checks: focus trap: PASS for modal, FAIL for persistent panel focus restore on close; color contrast for hint text: WARN; mobile hit targets: WARN. Uploaded artboard: keys-safety-v2.fig (https://design.redwood.local/file/keys-safety-v2)
